title: introduce-rag-telemetry-fidelity-matrix-playground-adapters
author: Maya Ortega
release_notes: Added a new RAG telemetry fidelity matrix and a small playground with adapters for TypeScript and Python. This introduces telemetry presets and sample probes to help teams tune metrics cost vs. signal tradeoffs without instrumenting production workloads.
description:
Motivation: teams building RAG flows need a reproducible way to evaluate telemetry signal fidelity (token-level traces, tool-call boundaries, index access markers) against ingestion cost and query latency. This PR adds a compact "playground" that demonstrates three telemetry fidelity presets (minimal, standard, verbose), a fidelity matrix document describing recommended signals and retention, and small adapter shims to wire the playground into TS and Python quickstarts.

What I changed: added a telemetry fidelity matrix doc under examples/playground/telemetry, a headless playground runner that spins up a local RAG sandbox with an instrumented proxy, TypeScript and Python adapter examples with run.sh and README snippets, and a small smoke CI job that validates telemetry events are emitted for each preset. The playground intentionally keeps dependencies minimal and uses an in-memory index for quick iteration.

Checklist: - [x] Add fidelity matrix and guidance docs - [x] Add playground runner and adapters (TS + Python) - [x] Add smoke CI job and fixture data - [x] Add examples to docs navigation (redwood-docs PR link in comments) - [x] Unit tests for telemetry probe helpers

How to use (quick): 1) cd examples/playground/telemetry 2) ./run_playground.sh --preset=standard 3) open http://localhost:3456/playground to run scripted scenarios or use the CLI runner: ./playground_cli.py --scenario=tool-fallback 4) Inspect emitted events in ./telemetry/out/{preset}.json or stream to a local endpoint.

Why this is unique: many existing quickstarts show RAG tool-calling and authoring; we lacked a small reproducible harness for telemetry cost/benefit experiments. This playground is intentionally opinionated: it captures a minimal set of signals by default and provides clear knobs to increase fidelity so engineers can reason about token-level costs vs. observability.

Related: Linear ENG-2143 (telemetry presets research), ENG-2209 (playground CI). Also references a companion docs PR on redwood-docs to add a short authoring guide and a telemetry best-practices sidebar (link posted in reviewer comments).
commits_summary: c1a8b9f: add telemetry fidelity matrix doc; 92b4d2a: introduce playground runner and in-memory index; 47f3e1d: ts and py adapter shims + readmes; aab2c07: add smoke CI job and fixtures; 8d5f2b1: tests and docs links
review_thread: Liam Chen (reviewer): Nice work, Maya. Can you reduce the default verbose preset retention window? Token traces balloon quickly and can confuse new users.
Maya Ortega (author): Good point, reduced verbose preset retention from 7d to 24h and added a note in the fidelity matrix about cost impact.
Anika Rao (reviewer): The TS adapter uses a small local WebSocket shim. Please add an example of streaming telemetry events in the README.
Maya Ortega (author): Added a streaming example and a small helper script to convert events to CSV for quick inspection.
Diego Martinez (reviewer): CI job failed on first run due to flaky test 'test_probe_backpressure' — looks like a timing assumption in the test. Please add retries or use a deterministic fixture.
Maya Ortega (author): Reworked the test to use deterministic fixtures and exponential backoff; re-ran CI and it passed.
